title: devbin reads cargo's build tree only from CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so a tree moved by CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR or build.target-dir is removed by fullcycle's clean and the check reads no tree, INCONCLUSIVE at rc 0
body:
FOUND 2026-09-25 by critic-shell's first pass on 0148 v1 (devbin-cc's build), driven with real cargo 1.98.1; filed into 0.1.8 on hv's ruling of the same day.

WHAT HAPPENS. cargo takes its build tree from three carriers: the CARGO_TARGET_DIR environment variable, the CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR environment variable, and `build.target-dir` in a `.cargo/config.toml` anywhere up cargo's config hierarchy. devbin reads only the first: cargo_target_dirs (lib/helpers) and 0148's guard look at CARGO_TARGET_DIR and nothing else. Driven: with CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR=rel/t run from a crate, fullcycle's clean removed crate/target, cargo built crate/rel/t/debug, and the check read "NO cargo build tree found", INCONCLUSIVE at rc 0 -- the outcome 0148 fixes for CARGO_TARGET_DIR, reached through another carrier. A config `target-dir = "out"` is unseen in the same way.

WHO IT REACHES. Measured by vc on 2026-09-25: nobody today. Neither variable is set in the fleet's environment, ~/.cargo/config.toml sets no target-dir, and no .cargo/config* under ~/Devel/prj (_Archive excluded) sets one. The exposure is to the first estate that adopts either carrier.

THE FIX FOR devbin, in 0.1.8. Ask cargo where the tree is rather than re-reading cargo's configuration in shell: `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` reports `target_directory` after every carrier has been applied, so cargo stays the one resolver. cargo_target_dirs and 0148's guard take their answer from it, and a failed or empty answer is refused by name before anything is removed. The pages (fullcycle, check targetdir, clean) name what is examined. The arms hold each carrier -- the two variables and a config file -- reading the tree cargo actually builds, and a refusal when cargo cannot answer.

## Resolution

Fixed at 57bcbde. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. devbin now reads cargo's build tree from every carrier. CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR is judged as CARGO_TARGET_DIR is, the one cargo puts first deciding. Where a `.cargo/config.toml` or `.cargo/config` naming target-dir or include sits in a crate's directory, above it, or in CARGO_HOME, cargo itself is asked where that crate builds -- `cargo metadata --offline --no-deps`, run from the crate, with neither variable in its environment, the paths read byte for byte -- and fullcycle judges and examines that tree, refusing before anything is removed a tree it cannot judge, cargo or jq missing, or a manifest cargo cannot read. With no such config, nothing changes and cargo is not run. check targetdir takes its verdict from cargo: a fork fails, its cause named where a config it can read accounts for it; one the machine's config alone causes, asked of cargo from a throwaway crate, is reported, not failed; a config no crate builds with is reported. A directory the walk for crates cannot read fails the check only when a config is in play over it, and is otherwise reported (vc's rulings). Tests are hermetic: an empty CARGO_HOME of each test's own.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD (parked for hv). fullcycle's refusal of a machine-config fork does not name the machine's config. A nested config pinning its own crate's target, over a hole with a second workspace beneath, is reported. A machine config with no crate answered counts as in play over a hole. The no-cargo-invocation arm reads lib/cmd/fullcycle's text only. `/` tidied to empty reaches cargo_place's status 3, unreachable while every caller refuses `/` first. A build line that runs cargo from another directory, or passes --target-dir or --config, can build elsewhere (declared).
- REVIEWS. critic-shell's passes on v1 to v2e, each warning built, converged at v2f; the guard delta converged. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-26, approved at v2g on the rulings built as ruled, the drives and the evidence below; the final suite over the landed stack is below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Each arm red at its own assertion against the code before it. 39 mutants at v2f, all killed on the land-order stack; U20, cargo_place's guard removed, killed at its arm's bound. Targeted: 461 ok, 0 not ok. Population: the fleet's 37 manifests answer, none builds elsewhere, 36 Cargo.lock files unchanged by the ask; no fleet config sets target-dir.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the six remaining 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on a252178 (0134, 0135, 0145, 0149, 0148, 0150), on a clean checkout built from the six exports (head 55f4c7e, tree 840726e0, the build stack's own tree), 2026-09-26 02:11:38Z to 02:46:47Z: 2040 of 2040 ok, 0 not ok, its 5 skips the declared ones (two no-tty branches, two require_command arms that skip off CI, the case-sensitive rename arm on this case-folding disk); the arms that need real cargo ran. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree.
